- Process Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the improved rule would have prevented the 21:53 patch from bypassing approval.
- QA Strategist tests the new rule by simulating a role-routing failure and confirming the exception-fallback path is invoked only after 2 PE attempts and produces a docs-only patch.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.

The rule must be referenced from bead-protocol.md.

Three observed exception-fallbacks: (1) 2026-07-12 20:52 Codex-Orchestrator docs patch after PE prompt-miss; (2) 2026-07-12 21:36+21:38 Documentation Reviewer via --actor flag because wrapper not invoked; (3) 2026-07-12 21:53 Codex-Orchestrator code/permission patch. title: Evaluate orchestrated agents on their own framework
description:
﻿## Context
Use the newly added orchestrated agents framework on a small but real task before using it on SocialHub product code.

## Actual Task
Have MiniMax-M3 roles review and harden the `.orchestrated-agents/` package itself. The evaluation should run the full workflow: role-selection debate, human-input gate, maker-only edits if needed, adversarial review, QA evidence review, security/privacy review, documentation review, and workflow-scout check.

## Why This Is Useful
This is low risk because it touches only the orchestration package, but it is real because it can find gaps in the wrapper, role prompts, Beads discipline, OpenCode permissions, and documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector comments the required role matrix and SDLC coverage.
- Human Question Framer confirms no human input is needed or provides a decision packet.
- Maker Engineer or Process Engineer makes only scoped improvements, if critiques require changes.
- Adversarial Reviewer, QA Strategist, Security Privacy Reviewer, Documentation Reviewer, and Workflow Scout each comment with evidence.
- Any process flaw creates a follow-up workflow-improvement bead.
- The evaluation records whether the setup is ready for product-code tasks.
acceptance_criteria: A full MiniMax role loop reviews the orchestration package and records evidence-backed approvals or follow-up beads.

comments.author: adversarial-reviewer
comments.text:
### Commentor: Adversarial Reviewer

**Step/Subtask:** Adversarial review - findings on .orchestrated-agents/ package (Part 1 of 2: defects and inconsistencies)

**Status:** Needs Fix

**Findings:** I read every file under .orchestrated-agents/ (README.md, bin/oa.cmd, bin/oa.ps1, docs/context.md, docs/beadbox-windows.md, all 10 roles/*.md, all 4 workflows/*.md, all 4 templates/*.md) plus opencode.json. The package is well-structured overall, but I am finding multiple real defects that need Process Engineer fixes before this can be approved for product-code tasks. Posting the full evidence now; part 2 will follow with the Approved / Needs Fix verdict once Maker/Process fixes are proposed.

**Defect A1 - Stale doc contradicts wrapper behavior:** docs/context.md line 62 says 'The wrapper also assigns and comments at invocation time, but that is a guardrail.' This is FALSE. The wrapper in bin/oa.ps1 (Run-Role function lines 186-258) does NOT call bd update or bd comment. It only sets BEADS_ACTOR / OA_TARGET_BEAD / OA_ROLE_NAME and spawns opencode run. README.md line 48 and roles/bead-protocol.md line 16 are correct; docs/context.md contradicts them. This will mislead future roles into expecting a guardrail comment that does not exist.

**Defect A2 - Maker Engineer permission too broad under --auto:** opencode.json lines 85-95 grant maker-engineer 'edit: allow' and bash '*': allow, with only narrow denies (git push, git reset --hard, git checkout --, rm -rf, del, Remove-Item). The wrapper spawns OpenCode with --auto (oa.ps1 line 249), which means every allowed command executes without confirmation. maker-engineer.md says 'Do not commit, push, deploy, migrate, or change secrets unless explicitly authorized' but permission does not block 'git commit', 'npm publish', Alembic upgrade head, or writes to .env. Role prompt is not enforcement. Need explicit denies for git commit, alembic upgrade, env-file writes, and any secret-touching file pattern.

**Defect A3 - Process Engineer permission blocks legitimate verification:** opencode.json lines 225-235 allow Process Engineer 'bd *', 'git status/diff/log', 'rg *' but deny npm/pytest by default ('*': ask). Workflow Scout and Adversarial Reviewer hand work to Process Engineer; if Process Engineer needs to verify a fix with npm run lint or pytest it must ask for each call. Either add lint/test as allow, or document that Process Engineer defers verification to QA Strategist and states that explicitly.

**Defect A4 - Security Privacy Reviewer cannot run secret scanners or tests:** opencode.json lines 151-158 grant Security Privacy Reviewer only bd/git/rg. No npm run lint, no pytest, no gitleaks/trufflehog. A meaningful security review of the orchestration package needs to actually run a secret scan and unit-test the wrapper. Add at minimum: npm run lint*, pytest*, and a documented allowlist for gitleaks/trufflehog.

**Defect A5 - Negative-then-allow permission precedence is order-dependent:** opencode.json roles use bash: { '*': deny, 'bd *': allow, ... }. Whether a rule like 'bd *' overrides '*': deny depends on OpenCode's matcher. If OpenCode evaluates pattern in declaration order and '*' matches as literal first, then bd never gets allowed. Need an explicit test of 'oa.cmd run ... adversarial-reviewer' executing 'bd show socialhub-v8g.4' to prove the precedence works. Same pattern repeats for every oa-* agent. Recommend documenting OpenCode's actual behavior in docs/context.md or testing each role once with a benign bd command.

**Defect A6 - README overstates portability:** README.md lines 56-67 'Copying To Another Repository' implies the package is portable. The wrapper itself (bin/oa.cmd + bin/oa.ps1) is Windows-only: oa.cmd uses @echo off, the .ps1 uses PowerShell SecureString DPAPI (Windows-only), and the spawn pattern uses %~dp0 and Read-Host -AsSecureString. README never says 'Windows-only' or 'experimental macOS/Linux support'. Either implement a POSIX shell wrapper or explicitly state Windows-only in the README and in docs/context.md.

**Defect A7 - System reminder points to uppercase CONTEXT.md while file is lowercase:** The orchestration package's doc path in the operating context is .orchestrated-agents/docs/context.md (lowercase). The system instruction I just received referenced .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md (uppercase). On Windows the case-insensitive FS hides this; on macOS/Linux the mismatch will break. README, opencode.json, and all role prompts reference lowercase context.md. Normalize the system reminder path or rename the file consistently.

**Defect A8 - Role-selection template is missing the Meta column it already needs:** templates/role-selection.md columns are 'Role | Reason | Maker Or Adversary | Required Sign-off'. The actual Role Selector comment on THIS bead (socialhub-v8g.4) used 'Meta' classification for Role Selector, Human Question Framer, and Workflow Scout. The template should be updated to add 'Meta' as a valid value for the Maker Or Adversary column, or split into two columns. Currently the template forces the role to free-text it.

**Defect A9 - scout-bead.md template is missing required Context / Acceptance headers:** Templates for new workflow-improvement beads (templates/scout-bead.md) include '## Context' but not '## Actual Task', '## Why This Is Useful', or '## Acceptance Criteria' which other beads in this repo (including the parent epic socialhub-v8g and this bead itself) use. Workflow Scout will produce inconsistent improvement beads. Align the template with the standard bead description shape.

**Defect A10 - Acceptance criteria for this bead is ambiguous about verdict ownership:** Acceptance criterion 6 says 'The evaluation records whether the setup is ready for product-code tasks.' No role is assigned this verdict. Workflow Scout files follow-ups; who declares ready/not-ready? Should be named explicitly (proposal: Workflow Scout synthesizes the verdict after collecting sign-offs, with Human Question Framer on standby for unresolved disagreement).

**Defect A11 - Permission allows Process Engineer to edit the wrapper that runs everything:** opencode.json lines 220-224 allow Process Engineer to edit '.orchestrated-agents/**' (including bin/oa.cmd and bin/oa.ps1) and 'opencode.json'. If Process Engineer makes a typo in oa.ps1, the next oa.cmd invocation could break before any role has a chance to review. Recommend at minimum requiring an Adversarial Reviewer checkpoint before any change to bin/** takes effect, or adding a pre-flight self-test inside oa.ps1.

**Defect A12 - Workflow Scout permission lacks 'bd close' for filing improvement beads:** opencode.json lines 205-212 allow git status/diff, rg, and bd * (which covers bd close). Actually this is fine on review; bd * matches bd close. No defect here, withdrawing A12.

**Evidence:**
- .orchestrated-agents/README.md (78 lines)
- .orchestrated-agents/bin/oa.cmd (4 lines, full read)
- .orchestrated-agents/bin/oa.ps1 (270 lines, full read)
- .orchestrated-agents/docs/context.md (216 lines, full read)
- .orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md (33 lines, full read)
- .orchestrated-agents/roles/*.md (10 files, full read)
- .orchestrated-agents/workflows/*.md (4 files, full read)
- .orchestrated-agents/templates/*.md (4 files, full read)
- opencode.json (239 lines, full read)
- bd show socialhub-v8g.4 --json confirms dependencies closed and assignee now Adversarial Reviewer.

**Required Next Action:** Process Engineer (or Maker Engineer if scope stays outside .orchestrated-agents/) proposes concrete fixes for A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 with file paths and line numbers. After fixes are committed, I will re-review and post Part 2 with the verdict. Workflow Scout should also pick up A1, A2, A6, A7 as workflow-improvement follow-up beads regardless of inline fixes, since they document process gaps. Security Privacy Reviewer should independently confirm A2, A4, A11.

### Commentor: Security Privacy Reviewer

**Step/Subtask:** Independent security/privacy sign-off on the three security-sensitive fixes (A2 maker permission width, A4 security-privacy-reviewer permission, A11 wrapper self-check adequacy) plus verification that the Codex-Orchestrator fallback doc patch introduces no secret values.

**Status:** Evidence Accepted (Approved with documented residual follow-ups F1-F8 + N3 owned by Workflow Scout)

**Threat/risk scope reviewed:**
1. Secret exposure - `MINIMAX_API_KEY`, `MINIMAX_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY` handling, wrapper status output, edit/deny rules on `.env*`.
2. Authorization and user ownership - permission blocks for destructive git/alembic/docker/npm/scp, maker edit deny rules, role-attribution trust in `BEADS_ACTOR`/`OA_TARGET_BEAD`.
3. Prompt/state/checkpoint leakage - wrapper does not inject secrets into prompts; only sets `BEADS_ACTOR`, `OA_TARGET_BEAD`, `OA_ROLE_NAME` env vars for the child `opencode` process.
4. Filesystem and shell safety - destructive bash deny rules on maker; wrapper self-check parses `oa.ps1` and validates `oa.cmd` shim existence.
5. Dependency and supply-chain risk - `bd` resolved via `Resolve-Exe` from `$env:PATH`; `opencode` resolved the same way; no fixed-version pinning in the wrapper itself (pinned `bd v1.0.4` documented in `beadbox-windows.md`).
6. Network/API handling - wrapper does not make network calls; only child `opencode` process calls the MiniMax endpoint (out of scope for this review).
7. Data retention and logs - wrapper never echoes the secret value; only `minimax_key_value_printed: $false` is asserted. `Set-MiniMaxKey` scrubs `firstPlain/secondPlain = $null` in `finally`.
8. Risky actions that need confirmation - adversarial/QA/security roles have `edit: deny`; the framework relies on the maker prompt + adversarial loop, NOT a permission-blocked-confirmation gate. Documented residual risk; not in scope to redesign here (F7 tracks the governance rule).

**A2 evidence - `oa-maker-engineer` permission (`opencode.json` lines 79-110):**
- `edit`: `*` allow, `*.env` deny, `*.env.*` deny, `.env` deny, `.env.*` deny, `.env.example` allow. Cross-variant `.env*` coverage correct; example file allowlisted.
- `bash`: `*` allow with destructive-action denylist - `git push*`, `git commit*`, `git reset --hard*`, `git checkout -- *`, `git clean -fd*`, `rm -rf *`, `del *` (ask), `Remove-Item *` (ask), `alembic upgrade*`, `alembic * upgrade*`, `docker push*`, `npm publish*`, `scp *`.
- Residual risk observed, not flagged: maker still has `edit: * allow` and `bash: * allow`. Denylist blocks the known destructive primitives; permission block cannot police every phrasing (`git commit -am`, `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit`, etc.). The framework relies on the maker prompt + adversarial review + Workflow Scout audit trail. Consistent with framework design.

**A4 evidence - `oa-security-privacy-reviewer` permission (`opencode.json` lines 156-182):**
- `edit`: deny (security reviewer is read-only by design).
- `bash`: `*` deny, `bd *`/`bd.cmd *`/`bd.exe *` allow, `git status/diff` allow, `rg *` allow, `npm run lint*`/`npm test*`/`pytest*` allow, and the three-family allowlists for the two secret scanners: `gitleaks*`, `gitleaks.cmd *`, `gitleaks.exe *`, `trufflehog*`, `trufflehog.cmd *`, `trufflehog.exe *`.

**A11 evidence - `Test-WrapperSelf` (`oa.ps1` lines 167-197):**
- Uses `System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser.ParseFile()` to parse `oa.ps1`; throws with first parse-error line number on syntax errors.

**Secret-handling evidence (`oa.ps1` lines 57-143):**
- `Get-SecretPlainText` (57-67) - `SecureStringToBSTR` + `PtrToStringBSTR` + `ZeroFreeBSTR` in `finally`. Proper DPAPI handling.
- `Set-MiniMaxKey` (109-132) - `Read-Host -AsSecureString`, double-entry equality check, `SetEnvironmentVariable("MINIMAX_API_KEY", ..., "User")`, `$firstPlain = $null` + `$secondPlain = $null` in `finally`, returns `minimax_key_value_printed: $false`.
- `Clear-MiniMaxKey` (134-143) - removes User scope via `SetEnvironmentVariable` + `Remove-Item Env:\` for Process scope. Returns `minimax_key_value_printed: $false`.
- `Get-MiniMaxKeyState` (69-86) - only returns `_present` booleans; never returns the value.

**Independent security conclusions:**

title: N3: Probe-comment audit-trail gate in bead-protocol.md
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a bead-protocol gap. Across socialhub-v8g.4, five probe-class comments have been observed: (1) 17:53 Role Selector probe x3 (short, no structured headings), (2) 18:01 HQF probe, (3) 20:55 Adversarial Reviewer probe, (4) 22:01 Workflow Scout tool-mechanic probe (this turn, self-acknowledged in the 22:02 substantive comment). The bead-protocol.md No Test Comments rule (per .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md) forbids probe / placeholder / scratch comments on real beads, but the rule is not enforced by any wrapper pre-flight or bd-side check. Comments can be posted without the required six headings (Commentor / Step+Subtask / Status / Findings / Evidence / Required Next Action) or the minimum-length that a meaningful Markdown work record implies. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named N3 as a follow-up; the 22:01 Workflow Scout probe is direct evidence that the gap is open.

## Actual Task
Add a Probe-Comment Gate rule to .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md. The rule must: (a) require every bd comment invocation to include the six required headings per .orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md (Commentor, Step+Subtask, Status, Findings, Evidence, Required Next Action), (b) require a minimum-length (e.g., the comment body must be \u003e= 200 characters or \u003e= 8 lines after the role author line), (c) reject comments that match probe-token patterns (e.g., 'TEST', 'Line 1', 'placeholder', 'scratch', 'scratch text', 'experiment', single-status-only comments). Enforce the rule at wrapper pre-flight (per F3) by extending oa.ps1 Run-Role to validate the comment body before passing it to bd. Reference N3 from bead-protocol.md as the source of the rule.

## Why This Is Useful
Probe comments on real beads pollute the audit trail. Future readers cannot distinguish a probe from a real work record without parsing prose for probe-token patterns or checking for the mandatory headings. The 5 observed probes on socialhub-v8g.4 demonstrate the gap. Closing N3 produces a hard-enforced rule that future probe comments are rejected at the wrapper pre-flight before being posted.

## Flaw
The current rule is documented (bead-protocol.md mentions no test/probe/placeholder/scratch comments) but not enforced. The wrapper pre-flight at oa.ps1 Run-Role does not check comment body shape. bd does not check comment body shape. The rule is purely aspirational. The 5 observed probes on socialhub-v8g.4 are direct evidence that the rule does not work as written.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future evaluation bead will accumulate probe-class comments in the audit trail. The audit-trail integrity guarantee erodes. Closing N3 produces a hard-enforced rule that future probes are rejected. The audit trail stays clean.

## Proposed Improvement
Extend bead-protocol.md with a Probe-Comment Gate rule (per the actual-task description). Extend oa.ps1 Test-WrapperSelf at lines 212-271 to include a comment-shape validation step that asserts any new comment on a bead matches the bead-protocol.md shape. Add a sibling pre-commit hook at .beads/hooks/pre-commit that re-checks the same condition (in case the wrapper is bypassed or the comment is posted via a direct bd invocation). Update Documentation Reviewer docs to reflect the new mandatory shape (the shape is already documented in .orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md lines 1-11; F11+N3 just add the enforcement). The probe-class exceptions (exception-fallback comments per F11) are explicitly whitelisted because they include the Why-This-Was-Necessary heading.

The rule must: (a) require every bd comment invocation to include the six required headings (Commentor, Step/Subtask, Status, Findings, Evidence, Required Next Action) per .orchestrated-agents/templates/comment.md lines 1-11, (b) require minimum-length (e.g., >= 200 characters or >= 8 lines), (c) reject comments that match probe-token patterns (e.g., 'TEST', 'Line 1', 'placeholder', 'scratch'). Enforce the rule at wrapper pre-flight (per F3) by extending oa.ps1 Run-Role to validate the comment body before passing it to bd.

Plus the Workflow Scout 22:01 tool-mechanic probe observed this turn. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named N3: 'four low-content probe comments on this bead ... bead-protocol gap; no security exposure ... but should be gated by minimum-length / structured-heading rule.'

title: F8: Process Engineer prompt-miss and role-routing anomaly pattern
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a recurring prompt-miss / routing-anomaly pattern. Across socialhub-v8g.4, Process Engineer was invoked 5 rounds (Round-1 at 18:05 closure, Round-2 at 20:43, Round-3 at 20:50, Round-4 Docs patch at 20:52, Round-5 no-op at 21:49). The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 comment claims 'I tried to route the fix through Process Engineer twice; the role ignored the explicit infrastructure-fix instruction'. The 2026-07-12 21:36 + 21:38 comments were authored with PE as the underlying actor but content authored as Documentation Reviewer - the routing-vs-content split is the same anomaly. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named F8 as a residual follow-up; Process Engineer 21:49 self-flagged the pattern as F8 candidate.

## Actual Task
Add detection and handling rules for the Process Engineer prompt-miss / role-routing anomaly pattern. The rules must: (a) detect a prompt-miss (a PE round with no editor commands or with a no-op comment that does not assign the bead to a new role), (b) detect a routing-anomaly (a PE round whose comment content was authored by a different role), (c) escalate to the Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback path per F7 after two consecutive prompt-misses, (d) close the loop properly when PE has no remaining scoped work (return a 'no-op handoff' comment, reassign to the next role in the convergence loop).

## Why This Is Useful
Prompt-misses can degrade the adversarial loop's effectiveness. Routing-anomalies break the audit-trail invariant (the BEADS_ACTOR must match the role that did the work). The 21:36/21:38/21:49/21:53 events demonstrate that without an explicit detection rule, the framework will silently accumulate the same anomalies on every evaluation bead. F8 closes the loop by making the detection explicit in the role-prompt and the workflow documentation.

## Flaw
There is no detection rule for prompt-miss or routing-anomaly. The 21:36 + 21:38 comments are syntactically valid Markdown work records but the actor tag does not match the comment content. The 21:49 comment is a no-op handoff that did not produce any editor commands because no Process Engineer work remained. The 21:53 Codex-Orchestrator invocation was triggered after 2 PE prompt-misses, but the rule that 2 is the threshold and that the exception-fallback can ONLY do docs was implicit. F7 captures the docs-only rule; F8 captures the prompt-miss detection rule.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future evaluation bead will accumulate prompt-miss / routing-anomaly comments in the audit trail. The audit-trail integrity guarantee erodes. The exception-fallback path becomes more likely to be invoked because the framework cannot self-diagnose the prompt-miss. Eventually, the framework will produce false evidence (process-engineer comments authored as a different role) that downstream readers cannot trust.

## Proposed Improvement
Add .orchestrated-agents/workflows/process-engineer-miss-detection.md as a new workflow file. The file must define: PROMPT-MISS SIGNATURE (round with no editor commands or no-op comment without bead reassignment); ROUTING-ANOMALY SIGNATURE (round whose comment content does not match the assigned role); ESCALATION RULE (two consecutive prompt-misses trigger Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback per F7); LOOP-CLOSURE RULE (after adversarial convergence, if PE has no remaining scoped work, return a no-op handoff and reassign to the next adversarial role); ROLE-PROMPT CLARIFICATION (process-engineer.md role-prompt explicitly recognizes the no-op handoff pattern and the role-routing anomaly pattern). Update process-engineer.md role-prompt with these explicit instructions so future PE rounds recognize the pattern and self-correct.
design: New workflow file .orchestrated-agents/workflows/process-engineer-miss-detection.md that defines (a) the prompt-miss signature (round produces no editor commands or produces a no-op comment with no bead assignment), (b) the routing-anomaly signature (round produces a non-PE comment from a PE assignee tag), (c) the escalation rule (any two consecutive prompt-misses triggers Codex-Orchestrator exception-fallback per F7), (d) the loop-closure rule (after the adversarial loop converges, if PE is invoked without a remaining defect, return a no-op handoff and reassign to the next adversarial role). Update process-engineer.md role-prompt with these signatures as explicit instructions.
acceptance_criteria: Documented detection rule for prompt-miss / routing-anomaly in .orchestrated-agents/workflows/process-engineer-miss-detection.md plus role-prompt clarification at .orchestrated-agents/roles/process-engineer.md
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. Process Engineer was invoked 5 rounds (Round-1 through Round-5). Round-5 at 21:49 was a no-op handoff because no remaining Process Engineer-scoped work existed. The same pattern was observed in the 21:36 + 21:38 Documentation Reviewer comments (author: PE, content: Doc Reviewer). Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 first named F8 as a follow-up.

title: F4: Per-role permission smoke-test scaffolding for every oa-* agent
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a missing automated verification step for OpenCode permission blocks. The Adversarial Reviewer Part 2 (2026-07-12 20:29) on socialhub-v8g.4 ran an empirical bounded-glob proof ( d show socialhub-v8g.4 vs  d show socialhub-v8g.4 --json) to demonstrate the declaration-order precedence rule. This proof is a manual, one-time test. Every future permission change to opencode.json must re-run a comparable proof, but no scaffolding exists. A2/A4 round-1 fixes (Process Engineer Round-1) added permission grants without re-running the empirical proof against the new rules. The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 exception-fallback patch widened  d ** permissions across 9 agents (lines 52-54, 77-79, 129-131, 154-156, 179-181, 209-211, 231-233, 253-255, 283-285) without any smoke-test to confirm no destructive subcommand regression.

## Actual Task
Add a permissions-smoke-test.ps1 script (and POSIX equivalent in the future oa.sh per F2) under .orchestrated-agents/tests/permissions/ that loads opencode.json, iterates over every oa-* agent, and asserts: (1) every llow rule actually allows the matched command; (2) every deny rule actually denies the matched command; (3) declaration order matters (a more-specific rule before a less-specific rule overrides; a less-specific rule before a more-specific rule is shadowed). The smoke-test must be exercisable by oa.cmd status --smoke-test and exit non-zero on any failure. The exit-code propagation requirement from F3 applies.

## Why This Is Useful
The Round-1/-2 audit cycle took 4.5 hours and 19 comments to converge partly because permission behavior could not be re-verified automatically. Every future permission change must be re-proven. The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 patch demonstrated that a permission widening can happen without an adversarial review because no smoke-test existed to even surface the change. With F4 in place, every permission edit produces a re-runnable assertion matrix that the QA Strategist must approve. The framework's confidence in its own permission blocks becomes evidence-backed, not assumption-backed.

## Flaw
There is no automated way to re-prove the bounded-glob empirical test on socialhub-v8g.4. The test was carried out by Adversarial Reviewer Part 2 manually. Future permission edits rely on operator code review alone, which cannot replicate the empirical proof at scale. Process Engineer's Round-1 permission edits were accepted by Adversarial Reviewer Part 1 via code inspection, which is weaker than behavioral proof.

## Impact
If not fixed, every future permission change is review-only. Process Engineer can ship a permission edit that LOOKS correct but BEHAVES incorrectly (e.g., a denylist pattern that does not match a destructive phrasing like git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit). Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 noted this as residual prompt-trust risk. The Codex-Orchestrator 21:53 patch added 9 multi-arg allow rules without a smoke-test, demonstrating the same gap. Closing F4 produces the only durable defense: a re-runnable behavioral assertion matrix.

## Proposed Improvement
Add .orchestrated-agents/tests/permissions/permissions-smoke-test.ps1 (and F2-port POSIX equivalent). The script uses Get-Content -Raw opencode.json | ConvertFrom-Json to load the config, iterates over gent.PSObject.Properties, and for each oa-* agent emits assertions like: 'agent oa-adversarial-reviewer: bash.allow.bd * - prove  d show socialhub-v8g.4 exits 0', 'agent oa-maker-engineer: bash.deny.git commit* - prove git commit -m test is blocked', 'agent oa-maker-engineer: bash.deny.rm -rf * - prove m -rf /tmp/foo is blocked (with a tmpdir cleanup)'. The script must handle three-family  d.exe / bd.cmd / bd resolution matching Resolve-Exe at oa.ps1 lines 25-34. The script must emit a structured JSON summary so the QA Strategist can review the matrix in a comment. Reference the smoke-test invocation from .orchestrated-agents/workflows/pre-flight-check.md (which F3 creates) so every CI run invokes it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Security Privacy Reviewer reviews the smoke-test for safe destructive-command proof patterns (the script must NOT actually execute destructive commands during the proof; it must use --dry-run or scripted verification).
- Process Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the smoke-test catches the empirical bounded-glob case from socialhub-v8g.4 and at least one additional round-trip case per agent.
- QA Strategist runs the smoke-test against the current opencode.json (with the 21:53 multi-arg widening) and confirms every assertion passes; the matrix is appended to the smoke-test output and shared in the bead comment trail.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: PowerShell script that loads opencode.json, iterates over every oa-* agent entry, and asserts (1) single-arg allow rule works ( d show socialhub-v8g.4 returns the expected fields), (2) multi-arg allow rule works ( d show socialhub-v8g.4 --json returns JSON, per the A5/N1 Adversarial Reviewer empirical test), (3) denylist works ( d create is denied for review roles). The script must be runnable via oa.cmd status extended mode and exit non-zero on any failure. Output is structured so QA Strategist can review the assert matrix from the comment trail.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke-test script at .orchestrated-agents/tests/permissions/ exercised by oa.cmd status; assertions for every oa-* agent role; CI-integration note in workflows/pre-flight-check.md (per F3)
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. The Adversarial Reviewer Part 2 (20:29) empirical proof ( d show socialhub-v8g.4 vs  d show socialhub-v8g.4 --json) is the only existing manual smoke-test. Adversarial Reviewer 21:23 closed A5/N1 with named evidence but did not codify a re-runnable test. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 carried F4 forward as Workflow Scout scope.

title: F3: Wrapper pre-flight --auto failure visibility (exit code propagation)
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a wrapper pre-flight visibility gap. Test-WrapperSelf (oa.ps1 lines 212-271) catches parse errors and missing shim, but the Run-Role abort at lines 313-316 throws silently. With --auto, OpenCode's interactive confirmation bypass leaves the abort invisible to the operator. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 named F3 as a documented residual follow-up on socialhub-v8g.4.

## Actual Task
Make the wrapper pre-flight failure mode user-visible when --auto is in effect. The current 	hrow at oa.ps1:315 inside Run-Role should produce a non-zero exit code AND a human-readable error message that surfaces before OpenCode spawns. Show-Status must also exit non-zero when Test-WrapperSelf fails so that oa.cmd status can be used as a CI-style guardrail. The same visibility requirement must apply to the future POSIX oa.sh wrapper (F2).

## Why This Is Useful
A silently aborted role invocation under --auto would surface as 'OpenCode ran but produced no actionable output, the bead was never assigned, and the next role in the loop gets routed to a previous-assignee bead'. The visible-failure pattern catches (a) syntax errors introduced by Process Engineer edits, (b) config changes that break Test-WrapperSelf, (c) permission changes that silently fail. Without exit-code propagation, every CI integration must grep stderr for an unrecognized error string - a fragile contract. Closing F3 produces a stable contract for wrapper pre-flight verification.

## Flaw
Run-Role at oa.ps1 lines 313-316 throws 'Wrapper self-check did not return ok. Aborting role invocation.' but does not exit the OpenCode child process, and the throw is captured by OpenCode's --auto handler as a soft error. The operator sees 'opencode ran', the bead is never assigned, and the next role invocation starts against a stale-assignee state. The pattern is not human-detectable without parsing stderr. Show-Status at lines 273-302 returns a JSON object that includes wrapper_self_check: ok or wrapper_self_check: fail: <reason> but does NOT propagate the failure as an exit code - so oa.cmd status always exits 0 even when the wrapper is broken.

## Impact
If not fixed, every wrapper pre-flight failure is silent. Future framework changes that break Test-WrapperSelf will produce 'bead appears stuck' situations that take operator eyes-on to diagnose. The CI integration story for the framework is fragile (must grep stderr) and the wrapper cannot be used as a smoke-test gate at the top of automation scripts. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 confirmed F3 is a real residual risk that the Round-1 A11 mitigation did NOT close.

## Proposed Improvement
Modify oa.ps1 Run-Role (lines 304-381) so that when Test-WrapperSelf returns != ok: (1) Write-Warning prints the wrapper_self_check fail reason, (2) exit 1 is returned BEFORE spawning OpenCode, (3) the bead is NOT assigned by the wrapper (matches the bead-protocol.md invariant 'the wrapper does NOT assign the bead'). Modify Show-Status (lines 273-302) so that if Test-WrapperSelf throws, the script exits 1 after emitting the JSON error object (so the JSON contract is preserved for tooling AND the exit code signals failure). For the future oa.sh POSIX wrapper (F2), apply the equivalent exit-1 propagation. Add a .orchestrated-agents/workflows/pre-flight-check.md rule that says 'every CI integration MUST assert oa.cmd status exits 0 before invoking any role' so the contract is codified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Security Privacy Reviewer signs off on the exit-code contract (specifically that an exit-1 from a wrapper self-check is NOT a secret leak).
- Process Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the improved behavior would have surfaced the A11 mitigation gap on socialhub-v8g.4.
- QA Strategist writes a smoke-test that intentionally breaks Test-WrapperSelf and asserts the correct exit code and human-readable message.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: In Run-Role (oa.ps1 lines 304-381), replace the silent throw at line 315 with an explicit Write-Warning + Write-Error + exit 1 sequence. Add a parallel exit-1 path to Show-Status (lines 273-302) so that oa.cmd status always exits 1 if wrapper_self_check fails. Mirror these exit behaviors in the future oa.sh POSIX wrapper (per F2). The visibility gap exists because --auto bypasses OpenCode's interactive confirmation, so a silent abort is invisible to the operator.
acceptance_criteria: Test-WrapperSelf failure exits non-zero from oa.cmd run and oa.cmd status; --auto invocation propagates the exit code to the parent shell; oa.cmd emits a human-visible warning before aborting even with --auto
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 named F3 as a residual follow-up: 'Test-WrapperSelf is parse-only and best-effort, but does catch the failure mode (syntactically broken oa.ps1) that would brick every subsequent role invocation. Wired into both Show-Status and Run-Role. Sufficient as a first-line guardrail; F3 captures the --auto failure-visibility follow-up.'

title: F1: Verdict-ownership rule for evaluation-bead acceptance criterion 6 (A10)
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a missing governance rule while auditing socialhub-v8g.4. Every evaluation bead carries an acceptance criterion 6 ('ready / not-ready for product-code tasks'), but no rule names which role owns that verdict. The verdict becomes orphaned at convergence time, blocking bead closure. Only the orphaning itself is observable, not the criterion check that would have prevented it.

## Actual Task
Add a 'Verdict Owner' rule to .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md (and optionally .orchestrated-agents/templates/role-selection.md) that names the role responsible for the acceptance criterion 6 verdict on every evaluation bead. The rule must default to Workflow Scout unless Role Selector explicitly assigns an alternate at intake time.

## Why This Is Useful
Four roles (Adversarial Reviewer, QA Strategist, Security Privacy Reviewer, Documentation Reviewer) agreed at 21:23/21:28/21:31/21:38 on socialhub-v8g.4 that the 'ready / not-ready for product-code tasks' verdict had no owner, and consistently attributed F1 to Workflow Scout. Process Engineer at 21:49 also handed off without naming a verdict owner. Without the rule, every future evaluation bead will hit the same gap and stall at the same convergence point. Adding the rule unblocks evaluation-bead closure across the entire framework.

## Flaw
The evaluation-bead template (inherited from .orchestrated-agents/templates/scout-bead.md Acceptance Criteria section) lists five role-level acceptance criteria but does NOT name a Verdict Owner for criterion 6. The role-selection template and bead-protocol.md are silent on the question. When the adversarial loop converges, no role is on the hook for the criterion 6 verdict, and Workflow Scout is implicitly assuming ownership by default - an unacceptable implicit design choice for a framework that requires explicit evidence-backed approvals.

## Impact
If not fixed, every evaluation bead will (a) require an implicit Workflow Scout verdict at closure, (b) fail named-evidence convergence because no role claims ownership, and (c) accumulate conflicting comments about who should have produced the verdict. The framework's appetite for evaluation beads will degrade as each one stalls. socialhub-v8g.4 is the first evaluation bead to hit this gap; future evaluations like socialhub-v8g.5+ will inherit it.

## Proposed Improvement
Extend .orchestrated-agents/workflows/bead-protocol.md with a 'Verdict Owner' section under 'Acceptance Criteria'. The section must state: (1) every evaluation bead declares a Verdict Owner in its acceptance criteria; (2) default Verdict Owner = Workflow Scout; (3) Role Selector may assign an alternate at intake; (4) convergence requires the Verdict Owner to post an explicit Approved or Not-Approved comment on the criterion 6 verdict before the bead can close. Update the role-selection template to remind Role Selector to set the Verdict Owner explicitly. Update scout-bead.md Acceptance Criteria template to include a 'Verdict Owner (criterion 6)' line. Backward compatibility: existing evaluation beads that lack the line default to Workflow Scout ownership at next convergence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Human-input gate runs and resolves any ambiguity about ownership (e.g., should the default be Workflow Scout, or another role).
- Process Engineer implements the rule only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the improved rule would have unblocked the A10 verdict on socialhub-v8g.4.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: Add an explicit 'Verdict Owner' line to the evaluation-bead template (or to bead-protocol.md under 'Acceptance Criteria') that names the role responsible for closing criterion 6 ('ready / not-ready for product-code tasks'). Default verdict owner = Workflow Scout unless an explicit alternate is named by Role Selector. Convergence rule: without a Verdict Owner line, the bead cannot close.

title: F12: Wrapper prompt template parity with new Test-WrapperSelf role-map
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a documentation/permission parity gap. The 2026-07-12 21:53 Codex-Orchestrator patch widened bash permission grants to allow multi-arg bd ** / bd.cmd ** / bd.exe ** across 9 agents in opencode.json (lines 52-54, 77-79, 129-131, 154-156, 179-181, 209-211, 231-233, 253-255, 283-285). The Run-Role prompt template at oa.ps1 lines 336-364 still teaches new roles to use bare bd show \u003cId\u003e, bd update \u003cId\u003e --assignee \u003cRole\u003e, bd comment \u003cId\u003e --stdin (single-arg patterns that were the norm before the 21:53 widening). The prompt template has not been revised to use multi-arg patterns that the new permission grants now permit, and does not teach the new role-agent verification capability added by Get-AgentName at lines 48-76 and the role-map validation at lines 237-263. Future roles will not learn that they can use bd show \u003cId\u003e --json for structured output, or that they can verify a role display name maps to a configured agent via Test-WrapperSelf.

## Actual Task
Revise oa.ps1 Run-Role prompt template at lines 336-364 to teach new roles: (a) use bd show \u003cId\u003e --json (multi-arg) instead of bare bd show \u003cId\u003e for structured output, (b) verify role display names against the role-agent map (Get-AgentName at lines 48-76) before claiming a role is available, (c) discover parent beads and dependencies via bd list --parent \u003cbead-id\u003e + bd dep list \u003cbead-id\u003e (replacing the current inability to programmatically traverse the bead hierarchy). The prompt must remain a complete, runnable example for new roles (so a new role can copy-paste it as the first command of the round).

## Why This Is Useful
The 21:53 patch updated the framework's permission grants to allow multi-arg bd invocations, but did not update the prompt template that teaches new roles how to use the grants. Without the prompt template update, future roles will not know they can use --json for structured output, role-agent verification, or dep traversal. The prompt template is the documentation that new roles actually read. F12 closes that gap so the documentation matches the capability.

## Flaw
The prompt template at oa.ps1 lines 336-364 is now under-spec'd relative to the new permission state. It still teaches single-arg examples even though the new permission grants allow multi-arg. Future roles reading the template will not learn the full capability. This is the same documentation-rot pattern as F6 (hardcoded count) but applied to a different file (oa.ps1 prompt template instead of CONTEXT.md).

## Impact
If not fixed, every new role invocation will be under-instructed. Roles will use the bare single-arg examples even when they could use multi-arg for richer output. The framework capability grows but the documentation stays frozen. Closing F12 keeps the prompt template in sync with the actual capability of the framework.

## Proposed Improvement
Revise the prompt template at oa.ps1 lines 336-364 to: (a) use bd show \u003cId\u003e --json as the first example (multi-arg) so new roles learn the structured output pattern, (b) include a role-agent verification example (e.g., 'verify the assigned role maps to a configured agent by checking bd role-agent \u003cRoleName\u003e or running Test-WrapperSelf'), (c) include a parent/dependency discovery example so new roles can navigate the bead hierarchy. Also update the wrapper status output at oa.ps1:265-270 to include a 'wrapper_prompt_template_version' field, so future changes to the prompt template are version-tracked. Documentation Reviewer must re-confirm the new wording matches the intent.
design: Revise the PowerShell here-string at oa.ps1 lines 336-364 to teach new roles: (a) use bd show \u003cId\u003e --json (multi-arg) instead of bare bd show \u003cId\u003e so they get structured JSON output, (b) use bd role-agent \u003cRoleName\u003e to verify the role display name maps to a configured agent before claiming a role is available, (c) use bd dep list \u003cbead-id\u003e to discover dependencies (replacing the current inability to programmatically discover a bead's parents and dependencies). Reference the new functions Get-AgentName (lines 48-76) and the role-map validation in Test-WrapperSelf (lines 237-263).

Documentation Reviewer re-confirms the new wording matches Adversarial Reviewer 21:23 + QA Strategist 21:28 evidence

The wrapper prompt template should be updated to use the multi-arg examples that the patch now permits. F12 is documentation cleanup that aligns the prompt template with the post-21:53 permission state.

title: F6: Replace hardcoded comment count at CONTEXT.md:197 with CLI verification
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a documentation-rot risk. The .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md line at approximately 197 (the BeadBox Context section, cross-referencing beadbox-windows.md) contained the literal phrase '21 inline comments' to describe the socialhub-v8g.4 bead. The count will go stale the moment any role posts a new comment - and the Workflow Scout 22:01 probe-comment + the Workflow Scout 22:02 substantive comment have already invalidated the literal. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 explicitly acknowledged F6 as a Workflow Scout follow-up: 'The replacement should be the verification CLI command (bd comments \u003cbead-id\u003e --json) and the success criterion (non-empty array), not a literal count.'

## Actual Task
Rewrite CONTEXT.md line 197 to remove the literal count. Replace with a verification instruction that uses the live CLI: 'verify bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json returns a non-empty array'. The text may keep its surrounding prose but the specific integer '21' must be removed. Confirm with rg that no other documented file in .orchestrated-agents/ contains a similar hardcoded inline-count.

## Why This Is Useful
Documentation-rot is one of the most common audit-trail defects: a literal number goes stale, future readers trust the number, and the discrepancy is not caught until a metadata review. Replacing the literal with a verifiable CLI command makes the documentation true-by-construction (any reader can run the command and verify the current count matches the description, which is the array being non-empty). The same pattern can be applied to F5's dates, F7's version numbers, F12's example command - any place a hardcoded value can be replaced by a live verification.

## Flaw
CONTEXT.md line 197 says '21 inline comments' as a current-state assertion. It is a snapshot at the moment of writing; the moment anything changes, the assertion is false. The same anti-pattern is in: beadbox-windows.md line 45 ('local bd v1.0.4 downgrade' - this is a version, also a rot risk if a future contributor bumps bd) and CONTEXT.md line 197 itself. There is no fix policy. The text is descriptive prose that is implicitly authoritative but explicitly mutable.

## Impact
If not fixed, the documentation will become a lie as the audit trail grows. The count '21' is already stale at the time of writing this Workflow Scout comment. Beadbox-windows.md line 45 will go stale the moment bd is re-upgraded. Future readers (and future Workflow Scouts) will misread the current state. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 confirmed the rot risk and recommended the CLI-verification replacement; this follow-up beads the implementation.

## Proposed Improvement
Replace '21 inline comments' with the verification instruction: 'verify with bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json that the returned JSON array is non-empty (audit-trail integrity)'. The replacement is a fixed string, not a snapshot, so it never goes stale. Apply the same pattern to any other hardcoded count or version in .orchestrated-agents/docs/ and the corresponding comment trails. Optionally add a style-rule to bead-protocol.md stating: 'Documentation must not contain literal counts or version numbers when those values can be replaced with live CLI verifications.'
design: Replace the literal count with a fixed-string reference to the verification CLI command and the success criterion. The text '21 inline comments' must become 'non-empty array from bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json' or equivalent. The relocation of the count to a structured audit-trail command removes the rot risk entirely.
acceptance_criteria: CONTEXT.md:197 rewritten to reference bd comments socialhub-v8g.4 --json non-empty-array as the success criterion; specific integer count removed; Documentation Reviewer re-confirms the new wording matches Documentation Reviewer 21:38 acceptance matrix
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. CONTEXT.md:197 contained the literal count '21 inline comments' which will go stale the moment any role posts a comment. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 explicitly ack'd F6 as Workflow Scout scope.

title: F5: bd v1.0.4 version-pin as a tracked decision bead
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a process gap. The bd CLI was downgraded to v1.0.4 to work around an upstream BeadBox comment-body bug (issue 27 at github.com/beadbox/beadbox/issues/27). The downgrade is documented in .orchestrated-agents/docs/beadbox-windows.md lines 45-50 and .orchestrated-agents/docs/CONTEXT.md line 197. But the upgrade/rollback decision trail is not recorded as its own bead. The doc describes WHAT was done, not WHO decided it, WHEN, or WHY. Future agents may upgrade bd back without context and re-introduce the same upstream bug.

## Actual Task
Record the bd v1.0.4 version-pin as a tracked decision bead. The decision body must include: (1) DATE the downgrade was applied; (2) SYMPTOM that triggered it (missing comment bodies in BeadBox UI; CLI confirmed comments existed; BeadBox log confirmed the UI bug); (3) PREVIOUS version (whatever bd was installed before the downgrade); (4) CURRENT version (bd v1.0.4); (5) RATIONALE for staying on v1.0.4 (upstream BeadBox issue 27 is open AND no bd release has fixed the comment-body regression); (6) EXIT CRITERION for re-upgrading (upstream BeadBox issue 27 is closed AND bd upstream releases a comment-body-safe version); (7) OWNER of the decision (Codex-Orchestrator or this role). Cross-link the decision record from beadbox-windows.md and CONTEXT.md sections so future readers find it.

## Why This Is Useful
A future contributor who runs bd upgrade latest will not know there is a pinned version below a known-bad upstream release. They will install the broken version, see the symptom, and lose hours debugging it. Recording the decision as a tracked bead makes the version constraint visible via bd ready and bd show. The exit criterion also makes the upgrade path explicit. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 confirmed the gap.

## Flaw
The downgrade is a one-line note in beadbox-windows.md and CONTEXT.md. There is no decision bead recording the upgrade constraint, the exit criterion, the date, or the owner. Anyone running bd upgrade today would silently roll back the fix. There is no automated check that bd is on v1.0.4 (the wrapper resolves bd via Resolve-Exe at oa.ps1:38 from env PATH, which allows any version to satisfy the lookup).

## Impact
If not fixed, the framework is one bd upgrade away from the comment-body regression. The downstream impact: every role comments would silently fail to surface in BeadBox UI; operators would see what looks like a complete failure of the adversarial loop. Many hours of debugging would follow.

## Proposed Improvement
File a decision bead under epic socialhub-v8g titled bd v1.0.4 version-pin (downgrade from upstream buggy release). Body uses the standard decision-shape: Context (the bug), Decision (pin to v1.0.4), Consequences (positive: works around the bug; negative: future contributors may not know). Cross-link from beadbox-windows.md:50 and CONTEXT.md:197. Add a wrapper-side guard at oa.ps1 Run-Role pre-flight (lines 304-381) that asserts the bd version is exactly v1.0.4 and exits non-zero (per F3 exit-code propagation) if it is not. Optional: pin bd v1.0.4 in opencode.json provider block by hardcoding the version, but that requires upstream patch - flag as F5-exit-criterion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Process Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the decision record would have prevented the bd-upgrade regression risk.
- QA Strategist verifies the wrapper-side guardrail (if implemented) exits non-zero on a non-v1.0.4 bd install.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: Use bd create --type decision (or chore, depending on Beads type registry) to record the upgrade/rollback/downgrade trail. The decision body must include: (1) the beadbox-windows.md symptom (missing comment bodies, link to upstream issue 27), (2) the current pinned version (bd v1.0.4 per beadbox-windows.md:45-50 and CONTEXT.md:197), (3) the exit-criterion for re-upgrading (upstream BeadBox issue 27 closed AND a release of bd that fixes the comment-body regression), (4) the owner of the decision (Codex-Orchestrator or the Workflow Scout role).
acceptance_criteria: Decision record at .orchestrated-agents/decisions/bd-version-pin.md with date, symptom, version-changed-from, version-changed-to, rationale, exit-criterion, owner; beadbox-windows.md and CONTEXT.md sections cross-link to the decision bead
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. The bd v1.0.4 downgrade is documented in beadbox-windows.md lines 45-50 and CONTEXT.md line 197 but no bead records the decision. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 confirmed F5 is Workflow Scout scope.

title: F2: POSIX oa.sh wrapper for orchestrated-agents framework
description:
## Context
Workflow Scout found a platform-support gap. README.md Platform Support section (lines 70-81, 70=heading, 72='Status: Windows-only.', 79='macOS and Linux are NOT supported by this version', 81='POSIX support is tracked as a follow-up bead') explicitly excludes macOS and Linux and references this follow-up. Without POSIX support, the framework is single-platform and any contributor on macOS or Linux must port oa.ps1 themselves.

## Actual Task
Implement oa.sh under .orchestrated-agents/bin/ with the same command surface as oa.ps1: status, key-setup, key-clear, un <bead-id> <role-name> [extra-prompt]. Port the role-name-to-agent-slug mapping (Get-AgentName at oa.ps1 lines 48-100) to POSIX shell-compatible syntax. Port the secret-handling DPAPI substitute to libsecret (Linux) and macOS keychain. Port Test-WrapperSelf to POSIX syntax (parse oa.sh with awk/grep). Update README Platform Support to remove the macOS/Linux exclusion and remove the F2 reference.

## Why This Is Useful
SocialHub is Linux-targeted in production (per AGENTS.md repo Boundaries), and future contributors may not use Windows. A Windows-only workflow blocks portability and excludes the most common code-author workstation OS. Closing F2 unlocks macOS/Linux contribution to the framework itself and aligns with the SocialHub product backend. It also forces a clean re-implementation of the secret-handling and self-check rules, which is an opportunity to harden them on Windows too.

## Flaw
The framework is bound to PowerShell 5.1 because oa.ps1 uses DPAPI SecureString conversion (lines 57-67 Get-SecretPlainText), PowerShell parse-based self-check (lines 167-197 Test-WrapperSelf), and PowerShell-specific scripting (here-strings, [Parameter()] blocks, [securestring] casts). None of these work in POSIX sh without re-implementation. The exclusion is documented but no implementation path is provided.

## Impact
If not fixed, the framework's contributor base is Windows-only. Any macOS or Linux contributor to SocialHub must either dual-boot Windows, run oa.ps1 under PowerShell Core / pwsh which has known DPAPI gaps, or operate outside the workflow. The framework cannot be adopted by non-Windows teams. Documentation Reviewer 21:38 acknowledged F2 as a real follow-up, not a documentation rot.

## Proposed Improvement
Add oa.sh under .orchestrated-agents/bin/ that mirrors the oa.ps1 interface. Implementation requirements: (1) role display-name to agent-slug mapping identical to Get-AgentName lines 50-76; (2) self-check that parses oa.sh and validates oa.cmd shim (or POSIX equivalent) and that every required role maps to a configured opencode.json agent; (3) secret-handling using secret-tool store (libsecret) on Linux and security add-generic-password on macOS, never echoing the secret value; (4) oa shim that detects Windows vs POSIX and invokes the right script; (5) README Platform Support section updated to remove the exclusion line and add a Compatibility section. The oa.ps1 stays as the Windows reference; oa.sh is the POSIX reference. Both must produce the same status object shape (role_agent_map, secret_present booleans, configuration paths).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Role Selector debate runs on this follow-up bead before any implementation.
- Human-input gate runs to confirm POSIX workflow preferences (preferred shell, keychain access, preferred  d install path).
- Security Privacy Reviewer reviews the secret-handling portability (libsecret / keychain) before implementation.
- Process Engineer implements only after required roles converge.
- Adversarial Reviewer confirms the oa.sh interface parity with oa.ps1
- QA Strategist runs an end-to-end smoke-test on POSIX (status + run <bead-id> <role>) and confirms the audit trail matches the Windows flow.
- Workflow Scout confirms the improvement is filed and discoverable from epic socialhub-v8g.
design: Mirror the oa.ps1 interface: status (returns role_agent_map and secret-presence booleans), key-setup / key-clear (using libsecret / macOS keychain instead of DPAPI), run <bead-id> <role-name> [extra-prompt]. Replace PowerShell here-strings with POSIX sh-compatible syntax. Use rg / git status / git diff / bd family commands the same way. The wrapper must NOT do the role work itself - only set env vars (BEADS_ACTOR, OA_TARGET_BEAD, OA_ROLE_NAME) and spawn opencode.
acceptance_criteria: oa.sh script committed under .orchestrated-agents/bin/ with status / key-setup / key-clear / run commands; smoke-test on macOS passes; README Platform Support updated to remove the macOS/Linux exclusion
notes: Discovered during socialhub-v8g.4 audit. README Platform Support section (lines 70-81) explicitly states 'macOS and Linux are NOT supported by this version' and points to this follow-up. Security Privacy Reviewer 21:31 did NOT flag POSIX as out of scope, and F2 is not security-sensitive at the design level; once oa.sh exists, the secret-handling rules from oa.ps1 lines 57-143 must be ported with an equivalent keychain-backed SecureString.
